subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should ClickClack use an unconditional 30-second completion deadline for JSON REST reads and mutating calls while multipart uploads remain exempt, accepting that a timed-out write may have reached the service?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically bounded and proven, but choosing the permanent deadline, ambiguous-write semantics, and upload exception is an owner-level transport policy rather than a defect with one objectively correct code repair.

options.title: Adopt the proposed REST policy
options.body: Accept the 30-second JSON completion deadline and multipart exemption, with callers treating a timeout after dispatch as an ambiguous remote-write result.

options.title: Narrow the request classes
options.body: Keep a deadline but specify different treatment or timing for read, mutation, and upload paths before revising the patch.

options.title: Keep current unbounded behavior
options.body: Close or defer the change if ClickClack’s service contract requires long-running JSON requests without a local deadline.

recommendation.title: Adopt the proposed REST policy
recommendation.body: Accept the 30-second JSON completion deadline and multipart exemption, with callers treating a timeout after dispatch as an ambiguous remote-write result.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the same ClickClack client provides the strongest available adjacent ownership signal for the timeout policy discussion.
